title: Projectile and Circular Motion
seo_title: Year 12 Physics: Projectile and Circular Motion Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Vectors and their components; projectile motion with independent horizontal and vertical motion; launch angle and range; uniform circular motion, centripetal acceleration and force; banked curves. (Senior Secondary Physics, Unit 3: Gravity and electromagnetism)
meta_desc: Free Year 12 Physics worksheets on projectile and circular motion: vectors, time of flight, range, maximum height, centripetal acceleration, centripetal force and banked curves. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Projectiles: horizontal velocity constant; vertical acceleration g.
key_sub: Circular motion: a = v²/r and F = mv²/r towards the centre.
body_html:
How to think about it

Treat projectile motion as two independent motions: horizontally the velocity is constant; vertically the acceleration is g = 9.8 m/s² downwards. Time links them. On level ground, maximum range is at 45° (ignoring air resistance).

An object moving in a circle at constant speed accelerates towards the centre: a = v²/r. The net (centripetal) force F = mv²/r can be friction, tension, gravity or a component of the normal force on a banked curve.

Example

Ball rolls off a 1.25 m table at 3.0 m/s. Time to land?

1.25 = ½ × 9.8 × t²

Answer: 0.505 s

Example

1200 kg car, 20 m/s, curve radius 50 m. Centripetal force?

F = mv²/r = 1200 × 400 ÷ 50

Answer: 9600 N

Common mistakes

  • Letting the horizontal velocity change during flight.
  • Drawing a 'centrifugal' force outwards in a free-body diagram.
  • Using the diameter instead of the radius.

faq.q: Why does a ball dropped and a ball thrown horizontally land at the same time?
faq.a: Both start with zero vertical velocity and have the same vertical acceleration, g; the horizontal motion does not affect the vertical motion.

faq.q: What provides centripetal force on a banked curve?
faq.a: The horizontal component of the normal force (plus friction if the speed is not the design speed).
